zip_caveats: ZIP codes don't follow Seattle's city line or its districts, so use King County's personalized lookup (My Voter Information, linked from kingcounty.gov/elections), your mailed ballot, or VoteWA.gov to see your exact races. City line: 98133 and 98177 include parts of Shoreline; 98146 is mostly White Center and Burien and 98178 is mostly Skyway and Tukwila, with only small Seattle parts; 98155 and 98168 are almost all outside Seattle and are left off this list. If you live outside the city, you don't vote on Seattle Prop 1, the District 5 council race or Seattle Municipal Court, and your District Court race is different. State House and Senate: most Seattle ZIPs sit in one legislative district, but these are split: 98103 (LDs 46, 43 and 36), 98104 (37, 43 and 34), 98105 (46 and 43), 98108 (37 and 34), 98109 (36 and 43), 98122 (37 and 43), 98133 (32, 46 and 36), 98134 (34 and 37), 98177 (32 and 36), with small slivers in 98107 and 98112. LD 11 does not reach into Seattle, even though it appears in the state pamphlet's Seattle edition. Congress: most of Seattle is WA-7; 98118, 98144 and 98178 are WA-9, and 98104, 98108, 98122 and 98134 are split between the two. King County Council (only Districts 2, 4 and 8 vote this year): 98125 and most of 98115 are District 1, which has no race; 98102, 98105, 98108, 98115, 98121, 98122, 98133 and 98134 are split. Seattle City Council: only District 5 (North Seattle: 98125, 98133, 98177 and parts of 98103, 98115 and 98117) votes this year. All Seattle voters share the same District Court race (West Electoral District) and the same Seattle Municipal Court races. Port of Seattle and Seattle School Board have no races or measures on this ballot. District shares come from our count of Seattle voters by precinct on King County's GIS maps.

dated.text: Seattle's vote centers, at City Hall and UW, are open: Saturday Oct 31, 10 AM to 4 PM; Monday Nov 2, 8:30 AM to 6 PM; Election Day, 8:30 AM to 8 PM. Any of King County's 24-hour drop boxes takes your ballot until 8 PM Nov 3.
